title: `geom_arrow_segment()` ignores `lineend`
description:
`geom_arrow_segment(lineend = "round")` has no effect. The `lineend` argument is accepted, but it never reaches the grob, so the shaft ends stay square. By contrast, `geom_arrow()` honors `lineend`.

Reprex
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggarrow)
library(grid)

# lineend stored in the grob's gpar, and number of vertices in the arrow polygon
inspect <- function(p) {
  gt <- ggplotGrob(p)
  find <- function(x) {
    if (inherits(x, "arrow_path")) return(x)
    kids <- if (inherits(x, "gtable")) x$grobs else if (inherits(x, "gTree")) x$children else list()
    for (k in kids) {
      r <- find(k)
      if (!is.null(r)) return(r)
    }
  }
  ap <- find(gt)
  c(gp_lineend = ap$gp$lineend, n_points = length(makeContent(ap)$children[[1]]$x))
}

seg <- data.frame(x = 0, y = 0, xend = 3, yend = 0)
pth <- data.frame(x = c(0, 3), y = 0)

inspect(ggplot(seg) + geom_arrow_segment(aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend), lineend = "butt",  linewidth = 12, arrow_head = NULL))
#> gp_lineend   n_points
#>     "butt"        "4"

inspect(ggplot(seg) + geom_arrow_segment(aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend), lineend = "round", linewidth = 12, arrow_head = NULL))
#> gp_lineend   n_points
#>     "butt"        "4"      # expected "round" and many more points

inspect(ggplot(pth) + geom_arrow(aes(x, y), lineend = "round", linewidth = 12, arrow_head = NULL))
#> gp_lineend   n_points
#>    "round"       "64"      # works
```

With `lineend = "round"`, `geom_arrow()` adds round caps to the polygon (64 points). `geom_arrow_segment()` returns the same 4-point rectangle as with `"butt"`, so the grob’s lineend stays `"butt"`.

Cause

`GeomArrowSegment$draw_panel()` has a `lineend` argument but does not pass it on when it calls `GeomArrow$draw_panel()`:

```{r}
GeomArrow$draw_panel(pieces, panel_params, coord, linejoin = linejoin,
    linemitre = linemitre, na.rm = na.rm, arrow = arrow,
    length = length, justify = justify, force_arrow = force_arrow,
    mid_place = mid_place, resect = resect, sep = sep, distort = distort)
```
`lineend` is missing from that call. `GeomArrow$draw_panel` falls back to its default, `"butt"`.

Suggested fix

Add `lineend = lineend` to that call:
```{r}
GeomArrow$draw_panel(pieces, panel_params, coord, linejoin = linejoin, lineend = lineend,
    linemitre = linemitre, na.rm = na.rm, arrow = arrow,
    length = length, justify = justify, force_arrow = force_arrow,
    mid_place = mid_place, resect = resect, sep = sep, distort = distort)
```

Session: R 4.6.1, ggplot2 4.0.3, ggarrow 0.2.0 (Windows).

title: distribute ggarrow on conda-forge?
description:
Hello,
Would you be willing to distribute ggarrow on conda-forge? Some relevant links on how to do this:

1. Conda-Forge documentation: https://conda-forge.org/docs/maintainer/adding_pkgs/
2. recommended helper script for bootstrapping submission of R packages to conda-forge: https://github.com/bgruening/conda_r_skeleton_helper
3. experimental Pixi build tooling for R packages destined for conda-forge: https://pixi.prefix.dev/latest/build/backends/pixi-build-r/ (the "Build process" heading on that page is a nice summary of how it works and its limitations)

If you're interested but too busy, I'm no expert but could probably put in an hour or so to try to get it working.

title: Next CRAN release?
description:
Hi @teunbrand,

Great work on this package. I have been integrating it into ggdag as an alternate backend to ggraph. It's so nice that I hope to make it the default someday.

I'd like to submit ggdag to CRAN soon, but the ggarrow implementation depends on the dev package. Before I try to work around that, I wanted to see what your timeline for your next submission of ggarrow is.

Thanks!

title: Feature request: implement wavy line drawing capability
description:
Currently, ggarrow offers the ability to draw  straight  and curvy lines. It would be incredibly useful to extend the package functionality to include the ability to create wavy lines.
I believe this feature would add significant value to ggarrow and make it an even more powerful tool for a variety of users.
Let me know if you'd like help refining this issue or adding more specific details!

title: Feature request: arrows for vectors
description:
I love the attention to detail in drawing arrows with {ggarrow}, and I'd like to be able to use that for drawing vectors, typically from the origin or grand mean in a variety of my plots.

`geom_segment()` can do this with the `arrow` arg, but the vectors aren't very pretty.

`gggda::geom_vector()` is the closest to what I'm after in terms of design for the interface (also allowing labels), but again the vectors aren't very pretty.

title: geom_arrow_segment bug
description: The second `if` statement in `GeomArrowSegment`'s `setup_data` reads `if (!is.null(data$resect_fins) && !is.null(data$resect_fins))`. I think the second condition should be `!is.numeric` rather than `!is.null`. This would make it match the check done on `resect_head`.

title: Feature Request: Two way arrows with half heads
description: Is it possible to implement arrows to show bilateral flows, similar to [flowmapblue](https://github.com/FlowmapBlue/flowmapblue.R)? Here, the arrows are cut in half (long ways), and each half arrow differs in size (not length) depending on the flow volume.

title: Feature request: support for linetype aesthetic
description:
Not sure if this package is under active development, but I've found it really useful so figured I would try opening an issue.

I've been using `geom_arrow_segment()` in a project and one limitation I've faced is not being able to set a linetype aesthetic. As a workaround, I've been plotting a `geom_segment()` with the desired linetype in one layer and `geom_arrow_segment()` with a significantly shortened length in a second layer. This works reasonably well, but it would be great if `geom_arrow_segment()` could have native support for the linetype aesthetic.

I completely understand if this package isn't a priority (especially given all your recent work on ggplot2), so feel free to disregard if that's the case. Thank you for all the work you've put into this package already, it's been a great help to me.

title: Visual bug: corners
description:
When points are spaced more densely than the linewidth, a glitch can occur at corners where a sharp angle transitions into a smooth curve.

``` r
library(ggarrow)
#> Loading required package: ggplot2
t <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 1000)

df <- data.frame(
  x = c(0.25, sin(t) + seq(0, 2, length.out = 1000), 1.75),
  y = c(2, cos(t), 2)
)

ggplot(df, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_arrow(linewidth = 5, colour = "white", stroke_colour = "black") +
  annotate("point", x = 0, y = 1, colour = 2, shape = 1, size = 20) +
  coord_equal()
```

![](https://i.imgur.com/LcwP1A7.png)<!-- -->
